_README: Single source of the book's structure; the build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Authored from book.draft.json (scripts/ingest_epub.py). The source EPUB splits every chapter into a numbered heading file (第X章) and a time-marker content file; each has been MERGED into one logical chapter here. Five pirate-site advertisement interstitials in the source spine ('读累了记得休息一会哦~') were DROPPED. Chapter ids start with 'ch'. A chapter is treated as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists.
description: Ma Boyong’s historical thriller unfolds over twenty-four hours (the twelve double-hours of the traditional Chinese day) during the Lantern Festival of Tianbao 3 (744 CE) in the Tang capital of Chang’an. A death-row convict, Zhang Xiaojing, is given one day to uncover and stop a plot to burn the greatest city in the world. This is an annotated English translation with footnotes, a glossary, and a translator’s apparatus.
_source_note: Source: digital EPUB of 《长安十二时辰》 (上下册), 马伯庸, 湖南文艺出版社 (Hunan Literature & Art Publishing House), January 2017. Original print ISBNs 9787540478315 (vol. 1) and 9787540478339 (vol. 2). The EPUB is a two-volumes-in-one file whose spine carries a numbered heading page per chapter followed by the chapter body; pirate-site advertisement pages in the spine were removed during ingest.
_translator_note: Rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note back-matter page.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 长安十二时辰 (The Longest Day in Chang’an) by Ma Boyong, made from the digital source EPUB.

The novel is built like a real-time thriller: its twenty-four chapters are the twenty-four half-shichen of one day, from the Snake hour of one morning around the clock to the Snake hour of the next. Each chapter heading names a traditional double-hour and its half; the English chapter titles gloss each one with its modern clock time so a reader can feel the countdown.

Notes are the translator’s throughout, except where a note explicitly marks the author’s own. Chinese personal and place names use pinyin, with conventional English forms kept where they exist. Genuinely ambiguous passages are footnoted, never smoothed over.
_structure_note: 24 numbered chapters (each a half-shichen of the day) plus two authorial afterwords. No sub-sections: each source chapter body is a single continuous unit. 'src' is the content spine href; 'text_file' the extracted source text; 'chars' the source character count of the body.
